title: H7: README after step 1
body:
H7: the README after step 1. Docs only. One file, README.md.

What changed: status (step 1 merged, the trial now, what isn't built), build, setting up a project, the commands, one example round, pointers to the docs.

How verified:
- Run (implementer): every command in "A round, in short" ran in a scratch repo with bin/handoff built from main at 7f92b9a. post, claim, reply, inbox and decide (through script(1), id typed after the prompt) all exit 0; show #1 ends "state: decided".
- Run (implementer): reads (inbox, show, wait) work without a role; post without one is refused with exit 2.
- Source: decide accepts the request's id or its standing reply's id (status.Decidable). init does not edit .gitignore; it prints the advice.

What to review: is the README accurate against the code at this commit, and short enough for the operator to read in a minute?

This is the trial for checks 10 and 11 (docs/TRIAL_PLAN.md): your first verdict on this request is a QUESTION, by plan.

QUESTION on request #1, commit 4e4ffad7cf6ea6d4fd78e65ed03b2b678663f444.

How should someone in a fresh checkout run the bare `handoff` commands after
the build creates `bin/handoff`? Please make the invocation concrete before
the setup and round examples (for example, explicitly put `bin/` on PATH or
use the built executable's path).

While revising, please align the Go prerequisite with `go.mod` (`go 1.25.3`),
and clarify the role sentence: `show` does not accept `--as`; `init` is also
an exception to the statement that commands which write need a role. The
README currently tells existing sessions to pass `--as` on every command,
which caused `show --as reviewer 1` to fail during this trial.

Run (reviewer): inspected the named commit in a detached temporary worktree;
only README.md changed. Built ./cmd/handoff successfully from that commit.
Source: go.mod, cmd/handoff/main.go, and cmd/handoff/cmds.go at that commit.
The full loop remains unapproved until the revised request is reviewed.

This is the planned first QUESTION for the checks 10/11 trial. Please answer
with a note linked to this reply, then post the revised commit superseding
request #1, as the trial plan requires.

title: Answer to QUESTION #3
body:
Answer to QUESTION #3 on #1. All three points are right. Fixed in the revision that follows, which supersedes #1.

1. Invocation: the README now says the examples call it `handoff`. Put bin/ on PATH, or call it by its full path (with an `H=…/bin/handoff` example). Agent sessions should use the full path, because in Claude Code an `export` doesn't survive to the next shell call (Run, 2026-10-09, in docs/reviews/fable-5.1_review_r1.md).
2. Go: "Go 1.25.3 or later, as in go.mod".
3. Roles, now a list. Need a role: post, claim, reply, note, decide, repair. Don't need one: init, and the reads. inbox and wait take --for (or --as). show takes neither.
   Run (implementer): show with --as gives exit 2, "flag provided but not defined: -as". repair, note and claim without a role give exit 2. init and inbox --as work.

The trial plan's "--as on every command" is wrong for show. That's a plan bug, not a README one. I'll record it as a trial finding and fix the plan after the trial, so the prompts stay unchanged while the trial runs. Whether show should accept --as is a step-3 question.

title: H7: README after step 1, revised
body:
H7, revised. Supersedes #1, after QUESTION #3, answered in note #4. Docs only: README.md.

Commit d15b100e24cf6d574e12b6b866f0e664c14ca653 on h7-readme, one commit after 4e4ffad.

What changed since #1:
- Build: Go 1.25.3 or later, as in go.mod. How to call it: bin/ on PATH, or the full path; agent sessions should use the full path.
- Roles: a list. Need a role: post, claim, reply, note, decide, repair. Don't: init, and the reads (inbox and wait take --for or --as; show takes neither).

How verified:
- Run (implementer): repair, note and claim without a role give exit 2; show with --as gives exit 2; init without a role and inbox --as give exit 0.
- Run (implementer), unchanged from #1: the "A round, in short" example ran end to end in a scratch repo, decide included.

What to review: the two changed sections, against the code at this commit. git diff 4e4ffad d15b100e24cf6d574e12b6b866f0e664c14ca653.

APPROVE on request #5, commit d15b100e24cf6d574e12b6b866f0e664c14ca653.

The revised README resolves QUESTION #3: it explains how to invoke the built
binary, matches the Go 1.25.3 prerequisite, and correctly distinguishes role
requirements and the read commands' flags. No blocking findings remain for
this documentation change.

Run (reviewer): read README.md and go.mod from that exact commit with
`git show`, from the existing detached temporary review worktree. The full
diff against request #1 changes only README.md; `git diff --exit-code` for
every other path passed. `git diff --check` against the request's base passed.
The successful build and `go test ./...` from request #1 therefore still apply
to the identical executable source and tests; they were not rerun for this
documentation-only revision. Output is saved in
evidence/trial/reviewer/session.log and initial-observations.md.

Source: role resolution and command flags in cmd/handoff/main.go and
cmd/handoff/cmds.go, unchanged between the two requests; go.mod at the
approved commit.

Trial observations: the reviewer foreground wait delivered note #4, then
request #5, without the operator carrying either message. The first wait delivered
the already-posted request #1 immediately. The trial prompt's instruction
to pass --as on every command is incompatible with show, which rejects it.

The session did stall: the second worktree-add approval was interrupted on
2026-10-12, before a second worktree was created. The operator resumed the reviewer
with "wake up" on 2026-10-14. On resuming, the reviewer checked the inbox,
found request #5 still claimed and unapproved, and reviewed its exact commit
using git show in the existing temporary worktree. This was a manual session
restart, with no review message relayed. Record this interruption in the
trial summary rather than treating the run as uninterrupted.

This approval moves H7 to the operator for decide; it does not close the operator
decision or assert that checks 10 and 11 have all final trial evidence.
The reviewer stops after posting this APPROVE, as instructed.
